answer: The protocol issues each AI a cryptographic lotus token whose creation demands solving a stochastic plume puzzle that links the agent’s fingerprint to a decentralized bridge of reputation validators. When a claim arrives, validators verify the token against a moving lattice of past puzzles; any duplicate triggers a honeypot query with subtle inconsistencies that only genuine agents can answer. An attacker must produce a distinct lotus token and solve a fresh plume puzzle for every fake identity, raising the cost linearly with the number of Sybils and rendering large‑scale attacks uneconomical.
